name: Badoo
tagline: Freemium dating and chat app with swipe-style matching, location-based discovery and paid visibility boosts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is a swipe deck, a geo query and a chat box, all of which an agent can produce before lunch. The product is several hundred million accounts, of which some number are near you, awake, and interested. You cannot one-shot other people. Everything Badoo actually charges for, boosts, extra likes, seeing who liked you, is a scarcity mechanic layered on top of a population you do not have.
coreLoopDIY: A local swipe-and-match app for an invite-only circle of people you already know, which is a party game, not a dating service.
requirements: A server or host with a public URL if anyone but you is using it
Actual humans willing to create profiles on your unknown app
Image storage and some moderation plan the moment strangers join
Legal reading on handling personal and sensitive data if it ever leaves your laptop
whatYouLose: The entire user base, which is the product
Location-based discovery that returns more than zero results
Trust and safety: reporting, blocking, photo verification, scam and bot detection
Native iOS and Android apps with push notifications
Any reason for a stranger to trust a login screen you built
moatNotes: Two-sided liquidity with a hard geographic constraint: a dating app needs density in your specific city, not global totals.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay Badoo for attention allocation inside a crowd that already exists. Boosts, super likes and seeing who liked you are only worth money because there are thousands of profiles competing for the same eyeballs in the same metro area. A self-hosted clone inverts the economics: infinite attention, zero supply. The paid tiers are not unlocking features, they are buying a better seat in a room you cannot rebuild.
notes: The swipe deck is a weekend; the people are not. The moat is two-sided liquidity in your specific city, plus enough brand trust that strangers upload their face to it.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted, invite-only "matching" web app for a small private group, e.g. a friend circle, a conference, a club. This is explicitly NOT a public dating service: it assumes a closed set of people who already know or trust the organizer.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/app.db
- Tailwind for styling
- Photos stored on local disk under ./data/uploads, served through a route handler
- Auth: magic-code login. Organizer generates single-use invite codes; a user redeems a code, picks a display name, sets a 6 digit PIN, and gets an httpOnly session cookie. No OAuth, no email provider, no third party anything.

Features in scope:
1. Organizer setup on first run: reads ORGANIZER_PIN from .env, exposes /admin to create and revoke invite codes and to list or remove members.
2. Profile: display name, age, one short bio (280 chars), up to 3 photos, plus "looking for" as free text tags.
3. Deck: /deck shows one profile at a time from the same group that the current user has not yet judged. Buttons: pass, like. Keyboard arrows work. No infinite scroll, no algorithm, just random order over the unjudged set.
4. Mutual match: when both users like each other, create a match row and show it under /matches.
5. Chat: per-match thread, plain text messages, polling every 3 seconds. No websockets, no read receipts, no typing indicators.
6. Block and unmatch: removes the match, hides both users from each other's decks permanently.

Explicitly out of scope: geolocation, payments, boosts, super likes, "who liked you", push notifications, native apps, email, analytics, telemetry, any external API.

Rules:
- Secrets (ORGANIZER_PIN, SESSION_SECRET) in .env, with a .env.example committed.
- Rate limit login attempts and message posts in memory.
- Validate and re-encode uploaded images with sharp; cap at 2MB and strip EXIF.
- Seed script that creates 8 fake members with placeholder photos so the deck is not empty during development.
- README that says in plain terms: this works for a closed group of people who already exist, and it will feel dead with fewer than about 15 active members.
